whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: A Filing Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. Claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as 6 months, so timing matters.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. This means compensation isn't artificially limited the way it is in some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they win or settle your case. This lets you pursue a claim without worrying about hourly bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Amador City?
items.answer: California law generally allows 2 years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity is involved, such as a claim tied to a public road, the notice window can be as short as 6 months, so it's best not to wait.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so partial responsibility doesn't prevent you from recovering compensation. Your final award would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Amador City?
items.answer: Public records show reported collisions concentrated along corridors like SR-88, SR-49, Fiddletown Road, and SR-16, with activity often peaking on Tuesdays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply public-record counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm ourselves. We connect you with an independent attorney, and if you choose to move forward, that attorney typically works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This is different from some other states, and an attorney can explain how it applies to your specific situation.
